newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish slightly higher.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished slightly higher, as the market reassessed Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments last week regarding the U.S. stock market.
"People are putting an overemphasis on Greenspan's comments," one Eurodollar futures trader said.

Traders again mulled over Greenspan's statements and concluded that the Fed would not tighten U.S. monetary policy to deflate U.S. stock prices. A Washington Post article on Saturday said that both traders and investors had misread Greenspan's "verbal signal" on U.S. stock prices.
However, one Eurodollar futures trader said that concerns about a correction in the U.S. equities market were leading investors to park money in three- and six-month bills.
"In terms of a more meaningful correction, it's continuing to provide a bid in two-year notes," he said.
If the stock market staged a substantial correction, traders would look for the Fed to lower interest rates to stave off the chance of a recession.
"A lot of people are taking Greenspan as a good factor," one floor trader said.

However, the advances in both the T-bond and Eurodollar futures markets were greeted with little enthusiasm in the pits. March T-bonds managed to climb above Thursday's settlement price of 114-15/32, but closed at 114-14/32, up 19/32.

At the end of pit trade, March 10-year notes were up 11/32 at 110-17/32, March Eurodollars were up one basis at 94.48 and June Eurodollars were up two basis points at 94.38. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
